parties: Plaintiff: No specific name mentioned
Defendant: 1st defendant (owner and driver of the private motor-car), 2nd defendant (driver of another car), and 3rd defendant (owner of the car driven by the 2nd defendant)

facts.F1: The accident occurred on 12th November 1968, when the plaintiff was pushing his cart across Castle Peak Road.
facts.F2: The plaintiff was injured when his cart and/or he himself came into collision with the 1st defendant's private motor-car.
facts.F3: The Statement of Claim recited two collisions, the first between the car owned and driven by the 1st defendant and a car driven by the 2nd defendant and owned by the 3rd defendant; the second collision recited was one between the plaintiff and the motor-car owned and driven by the 1st defendant.
facts.F4: At the hearing, the only evidence as to the actual collision was given by the plaintiff who said that he saw no second car and knew nothing of any collision between two cars.
facts.F5: The 1st defendant admitted to a collision between his motor-car and the plaintiff's cart upon the pleadings.
facts.F6: The plaintiff was taking a route across Castle Peak Road at a point without a zebra crossing, however another zebra crossing was available a short distance away.
facts.F7: The plaintiff waited about one minute for a number of cars to pass, and estimated the 1st defendant's car was at a distance of 200 yards (600 feet) from him when he started to push his cart across the road.
facts.F8: The 1st defendant's car had ample time to slow down and stop to let the plaintiff pass, but failed to do so, hitting the plaintiff.
facts.F9: The 1st defendant has not given evidence, and therefore did not dispute that his car collided with the plaintiff.
facts.F10: The plaintiff suffered injuries in the accident, including a partial rupture of the Achilles tendon of his left leg.
facts.F11: The plaintiff's claim for total loss of earnings for five months was not supported by evidence.
facts.F12: With proper treatment, the plaintiff would have made a full recovery by the date of the trial.

facts.F4: The applicant was responsible for repairing vehicles and for cleaning and tidying the Garage when required.
facts.F5: The respondent would notify the applicant if there were any problems with his customer’s vehicles and would instruct the applicant to inspect or repair the customer’s vehicles.

facts.F1: The companies Texxan Industries Limited (Texxan) and Chino Industries Limited (Chino) were incorporated on 27th March 1981.
facts.F2: In June 1988, the companies became wholly owned by Texxan Consolidated Limited, a Bermuda company beneficially owned by the petitioner and the Yue Xiu group.
facts.F3: The Yue Xiu group claims that Texxan is indebted to them for $157,000,000 and Chino for $95,000,000.
facts.F4: The petitioner claims a sum of $836,000 from Texxan and $136,000 from Chino.
facts.F5: The companies are alleged to be insolvent and unable to pay their debts.

facts.F7: The Yue Xiu directors appointed MR Nacson and EM McMillan as joint provisional liquidators on 8th March 1990.
facts.F8: The joint liquidators were appointed as joint liquidators by a majority in value of the alleged aggregate value of debts of the Yue Xiu companies and its supporters at the first meeting of creditors on 3rd April 1990.

facts.F12: A test for bias was considered in R. v. Liverpool City Justices Ex-parte Topping [1983]1 WLR 119, which is whether there is the appearance of bias rather than whether there is actual bias.
facts.F13: The balance of convenience may be influenced by the possibility of waste and duplication of efforts if a new provisional liquidator was appointed.

requested_remedy: damages for injuries to his right eye
parties: Plaintiff: CHAN KWOK PING
Defendant: HOP YICK ENGINEERING COMPANY and ABLE ENGINEERING COMPANY LIMITED

facts.F1: The Plaintiff was an employee of the 1st Defendant, a building contractor.
facts.F2: The 2nd Defendant was the principal contractor at the site.
facts.F3: The Plaintiff was instructed to paint the ceiling and walls of the building with white wash using a 5 foot spraygun.
facts.F4: On 9th November 1990, the Plaintiff started work at the staircase, where the pump was left about 20 feet away.
facts.F5: After starting work, the Plaintiff discovered the gun was blocked and squatted down to clear the nozzle with a pin.
facts.F6: The Plaintiff said he did not know why white wash came to be splashed to his eyes, but the likely cause was the white wash being diverted by the pin and his fingers.
facts.F7: The accident resulted in the Plaintiff suffering a large corneal ulcer, which was subsequently healed, resulting in a vascularised corneal scar and reduced visual acuity in the right eye.
facts.F8: The Plaintiff returned to work after the accident but could only work 15 days per month due to his eye injury.
facts.F9: The pump was left about 20 feet away from the Plaintiff when he started painting.
facts.F10: The Plaintiff did not turn off the pump before clearing the nozzle.
facts.F11: The Plaintiff knew that it was the practice to wear goggles when painting with white wash, but goggles were not provided by the Defendants.

facts.F1: The plaintiff, A.A. Albery & Sons Limited, issued a writ against the defendants, alleging that certain words published in the South China Morning Post were defamatory.

facts.F3: The plaintiff seeks an interlocutory injunction to restrain the defendants from publishing words to the effect that the plaintiff is a swindler.

facts.F7: The defendants swore that they would justify the words complained of and that they were fair comment upon the actions of the plaintiff.
